title: 4 Lines Series #7
description: Opposite corners begin together. The puck moves through two stationary outlets while the original player circles through center, transitions backward to receive, controls the puck while moving backward, transitions forward and completes another give-and-go before shooting.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through every transition.
Control the puck while skating backward.
Pass firmly to moving targets.
Transition forward without losing speed.

title: Finland 3 on 0 Re-Group
description: Three forwards break out, support one another through the neutral zone and regroup with a defenseman moving backward. The group then attacks with speed, with one forward driving the net and the other two filling support lanes.
coaching_points: Accurate passes and timing make the drill work.
Defense keeps the feet moving while receiving backward.
Forwards support underneath the puck through the regroup.
Enter with speed and finish with all three players at the net.

title: Defensive Zone Exchange Drill
description: Two defenders manage alternating low-zone 1-on-1 pressure as the puck moves behind the net from corner to corner. The defender protecting the front of the net stays until the partner has fully returned and relieved that responsibility.
coaching_points: Never leave the net front uncovered during the exchange.
Communicate the handoff clearly.
Corner defender contains the puck carrier.
Net-front defender protects the dangerous player until relief arrives.

title: Money Maker Drill
description: A forward retrieves low and feeds a defenseman, who moves off the wall and reads a one-time option to the back post. The forward then works behind the net on the next puck and attacks either side for another scoring chance.
coaching_points: Defense receives and moves off the wall before deciding.
Back-post forward times the one-timer route.
Low forward gets the puck off the boards quickly.
Attack both sides of the net to avoid becoming predictable.

title: Shot, Recover, Rebound Goalie Drill
description: A shooter releases from the high slot, then immediately attacks a pre-positioned puck beside the net as if it were the rebound. The goalie must recover from the first save and set for the second shot.
coaching_points: Goalie establishes angle and set position for the first shot.
Recover immediately after the save.
Track the shooter's movement to the rebound puck.
Shooter replaces the side puck after the repetition.

title: Neutral Zone Horse Shoe
description: Four lines are positioned at the blue lines. Diagonal lines go together: the first player skates up the wall to the red line, crosses laterally, receives a pass from the opposite line and then attacks the zone for a shot.
coaching_points: Call for the puck and show a target while crossing the red line.
Do not turn up ice before receiving the pass.
Passers hit the moving target in stride.
Keep both sides synchronized.

title: Forehand Retriever Drill
description: A defenseman starts near the top of the circle, transitions toward middle ice, then opens to retrieve a coach-dumped puck on the forehand. After collecting at an angle and facing up ice, the player carries to the dot and returns the puck to the coach.
coaching_points: Shoulder-check before reaching the puck.
Approach at an angle to preserve speed.
Open up without unnecessary crossovers.
Face up ice quickly after possession.
Add upper- and lower-body fakes as players improve.

title: Stretch and Go Flow w/ Backcheck
description: One player carries up the wall and finds a teammate stretching through the neutral zone. The receiver delays on entry while the passer catches the play for a high-slot return pass and shot. On the next whistle, the previous shooter becomes the backchecker.
coaching_points: Stretch player receives with speed.
Use a delay to let support arrive.
Passer works hard to become the high-slot option.
Shooter stops at the net, then immediately backchecks the next repetition.

title: Figure Eight Passing and Shooting Station #2
description: A player uses two tight cones for control turns, passes to the coach, transitions backward to receive the return, then moves around the second cone, gets another return pass and makes a lateral move before shooting.
coaching_points: Keep the feet moving after every turn.
Transition backward under control while receiving.
Sell the final shoulder fake before moving laterally.
Release the shot immediately after the lateral move.

title: Figure Eight Passing and Shooting Station #1
description: The player passes to a coach, skates around the first cone and receives the return, immediately one-touches the puck back, circles the second cone and receives again before making a deceptive lateral move and shooting.
coaching_points: Head stays up on the passes.
Feet accelerate out of each control turn.
Use one-touch passing when skill allows.
Make the deceptive move and shoot immediately.

title: Cross Over Passing Station
description: Two players weave around two nets while exchanging passes between the nets and using forehand drop passes behind them. The pair finishes at the opposite end and changes lines so both players work each passing role.
coaching_points: Passes between the nets are made in stride.
Drop the puck into space rather than passing it hard.
Set the drop so the receiver collects on the forehand.
Maintain spacing through the crossovers.

title: Box Out 2 on 2
category: Net Front / Box Out / Point Shot
description: Two attackers retrieve a puck and move it to the point for a shot while two defenders battle to clear sightlines and eliminate sticks in front. The coach can reload two or three pucks so each group gets repeated net-front reps.
coaching_points: Defenders establish inside body position before the shot.
Eliminate sticks and let the goalie see the puck.
Attackers create screens, tips and rebounds.
Point shooter works both a middle walk and a wall shot.

title: Swing Through Shooting Station
description: A player skates between two cones, picks up a puck and escapes up the wall. At each cone the player makes a single lateral shift away from the net, with the second shift loading the puck into shooting position.
coaching_points: Control the puck while moving laterally.
Use a clean single shift at each cone.
Second shift should place the puck immediately into the shooting window.
Backhand-side players can shoot backhand or open to the forehand.

title: 2 vs 1 Rebound Battle Drill
description: The goalie plays an initial puck into a corner, sending two players into a loose-puck battle. The winner moves the puck back to the point and the play immediately becomes a live 2-on-1 to the net.
coaching_points: Battle through body position rather than reaching.
Winner protects the puck, gets the head up and finds the point.
Point player moves to become a clear outlet.
Defender protects middle ice and forces a lower-quality shot.
Goalie tracks the battle, point pass and immediate 2-on-1.

title: Bumper Shooting
description: A coach shoots through or over two tires placed in front of the goalie. Two rebound players wait beside the tires to attack loose pucks, forcing the goalie to react quickly and square up to the second shot.
coaching_points: Track the first release through traffic.
React immediately to rebounds off the tires.
Square the body to the rebound shooter before the second save.
With developing goalies, require the rebounder to take one stickhandle before shooting.

title: Wild Half Ice Shooting Drill
description: A forward works through three pucks: first a rush shot, then a pass to the point followed by a screen or tip, and finally a high-roll exchange with the defenseman that produces a high-slot chance.
coaching_points: Forward follows the first shot for a rebound.
Point player walks inside the dots before releasing the shot.
Net-front player screens, tips and hunts rebounds.
On the third puck, time the high roll so both players finish at the net.

title: Respect 2 on 0 Goalie Drill
category: Goalie / 2 on 0 / Read Shot or Pass
description: Two attackers cross around staggered pylons after an opening pass and use a forehand drop. The puck carrier then attacks with the option to shoot or pass to the teammate driving the net, forcing the goalie to respect both threats.
coaching_points: Puck carrier disguises the pass by maintaining a shooting posture.
Net driver stays available as a backdoor option.
Goalie remains patient and square to the puck.
Do not cheat toward the pass before the puck carrier commits.

title: Post to Post Attack
description: The goalie starts set on one post, shuffles across the goal line to the opposite post, then moves to the top of the crease with a shuffle or T-push and gets set for a coach's shot.
coaching_points: Stay balanced during the post-to-post transfer.
Use controlled feet rather than reaching.
Arrive square at the top of the crease.
Be fully set before the shot is released.

title: Coaches Screen Battle
description: A coach stands in the goalie's sightline and applies light disruption. When the screen clears, the goalie must recover balance, find the puck and get square and set before the shot.
coaching_points: Stay calm while vision is obstructed.
Recover the feet under control when the screen clears.
Track first instead of guessing.
Arrive square and set before reacting to the shot.

title: Net Play Goalie Drill - 1 on 0
description: A forward rims the puck behind the net. The goalie leaves the crease, controls it and makes an outlet pass to that same forward, then must recover to the crease before the forward loops around a cone and attacks 1-on-0.
coaching_points: Goalie controls the rim before passing.
Make a hard, accurate outlet pass.
Recover orientation and crease position immediately after releasing the puck.
Forward attacks quickly enough to challenge the goalie's recovery.

title: 3 Level 2 on 0
description: Pairs leave from both corners and use three different cone depths to create 2-on-0 attacks. The puck carrier can pass to the partner or occasionally shoot to keep the goalie from overplaying the pass.
coaching_points: Pairs keep proper spacing around each cone.
Read the goalie instead of forcing the pass.
At the deepest level, use more than one pass when possible.
Goalie stays patient and respects both shot and pass.

title: Goal Line Options 1 vs. 0 & 2 vs. 0
description: An attacker receives a pass and loops around a low cone with several options: attack in front, fake and stuff the puck from behind the net, or feed a return pass out front. A second attacker can be added to create a cross-crease option.
coaching_points: Goalie holds the post and angle without cheating.
Track whether the attacker stays in front or goes behind the net.
Recover quickly to passes back into the slot.
With the second attacker, respect the cross-crease threat.

title: The Goalie Gauntlet
description: Several attackers move the puck quickly around the zone, ideally with one-touch passes. Any player may shoot at any time, forcing the goalie to track laterally and stay ready rather than anticipating a fixed final shooter.
coaching_points: Goalie tracks the puck instead of guessing the end point.
Move laterally with control and stay square.
Attackers keep passes quick and unpredictable.
Any open shooter can release immediately.

title: Shot Shot Stuff
description: Attackers work from several locations around the net, creating consecutive shots and a low stuff option. The goalie repeatedly adjusts angle and depth, then recovers across the crease for the next threat.
coaching_points: Goalie gets square before each release.
Recover through the middle rather than lunging.
Shooters hit the net and can progress to one-timers.
Keep work intervals short enough to preserve technique.

title: Square Passing
description: Four attackers surround the goalie and may pass as much as they want before any player chooses to shoot or attack from behind the net. The goalie must stay connected to the puck and be ready for a shot at any moment.
coaching_points: Goalie stays square and moves with every pass.
Use the stick to take away passing lanes when possible.
Do not overcommit before the shooter reveals the play.
Attackers keep the puck moving to challenge the goalie's feet.

title: Side to Side Quickies
description: The first shooter targets the far lower corner to create a controlled rebound. After the save, the goalie must recover hard to the far post for a second shot from a player stationed near that post.
coaching_points: First save directs the rebound away from the middle.
Recover to the far post immediately after the save.
Second shooter waits until the goalie has a realistic chance to set.
Switch sides each repetition and use short sets.

title: Double Attack from Corner
description: The goalie starts facing a coach in the slot while two attackers work from opposite corners near the goal line. The coach starts the play to either side, and the attackers can use a one-time cross-crease pass, a short-side attack or an extra pass to move the goalie.
coaching_points: Goalie tracks the initial pass and gets set quickly.
Respect both short-side and cross-crease threats.
Attackers keep the puck near the goal line until the play develops.
Limit reps so the goalie stays sharp.

title: Corner To Slot Shot
description: A coach or player in the corner feeds one of two forwards in the slot. The receiving forward may shoot or make one pass to the other forward, forcing the goalie to set quickly and read whether the play stays on the puck or moves laterally.
coaching_points: Goalie sets before each repetition begins.
Track the first pass into the slot.
Do not cheat toward the second forward.
Recover immediately after each shot before the next puck is released.

title: Bandits Goalie Drill
description: The goalie starts by dropping as if making a save, recovers to the feet for two slot shots, then handles a shot from beside the net before reading a final attack from behind the net that can come to either post.
coaching_points: Recover to the feet quickly after the opening drop.
Get set for each of the two slot shots.
Reset angle for the side shot.
On the final puck, track behind the net and seal the correct post.

title: Clear Conditioning
description: The goalie repeatedly leaves the crease to reach loose pucks and clear them to a designated target up ice. The drill builds conditioning while reinforcing decisive puck handling under time pressure.
coaching_points: Explode out of the crease without hesitation.
Arrive under control before playing the puck.
Use a clear target such as the red line or far blue line.
Prioritize a hard, accurate clear over simply moving the puck.

title: Goal Line Stand
description: The puck starts behind the net and is passed to either attacker stationed along the goal line. The receiver can attack the net directly or use the opposite-side forward as a cross-crease option.
coaching_points: Goalie reads the play as it develops from behind the net.
Stay connected to the near post until the puck moves.
Respect both the direct attack and the cross-crease pass.
Track the puck through the entire goal-line sequence.

title: 7 Man Rebound Drill
description: A designated shooter intentionally targets the goalie's pads to create a rebound while surrounding players race to the loose puck. The first player to reach the rebound gets the scoring attempt.
coaching_points: Shooter creates a playable rebound instead of shooting to score.
Goalie controls rebound direction whenever possible.
Players compete through the loose puck.
Rotate positions after a short set so the goalie stays fresh.

title: Rapid Fire
description: Players surround the zone and move the puck rapidly from player to player, with the restriction that the receiver cannot simply return it to the adjacent option. Any open player can shoot, forcing the goalie to track constant puck movement.
coaching_points: Keep passes and releases quick.
Goalie moves with every pass and stays square.
Any shooter can attack when the lane opens.
Use short rep blocks and rotate the initiating passer or goalie.

title: Goalie Line Sumo Wrestling
description: Two goalies begin on their knees on opposite sides of a line and apply controlled pressure against one another, trying to move the opponent across the boundary while maintaining strong posture and balance.
coaching_points: Stay upright through the core.
Use controlled knee pushes instead of lunging.
Keep weight balanced through contact.
Progress to a faceoff-circle boundary to increase the challenge.

title: Davos Game
description: A full-length, one-third-ice game where two teams play with almost no restrictions. The long narrow area encourages creative passing, skating into space, communication and quick counterattacks.
coaching_points: Players plan ahead before entering the game.
Communicate constantly in the open-format environment.
Use bank passes and area passes to create separation.
Defenders angle with sticks in lanes.
Goalies can help start attacks with puck movement.

title: Trucks & Trailers Warm-Up
description: Players work in pairs. One player leads with skating and skill movements while the partner mirrors every move. Roles switch frequently, and the activity can progress from no pucks to both players handling pucks.
coaching_points: Keep the head up and scan constantly.
Leader uses real hockey movements rather than random skating.
Follower reacts while staying aware of traffic.
Shrink the space or add pucks to increase difficulty.

title: Head Up Scan The Ice Warm-Up
description: Players move through a designated area with the puck, changing direction on whistles and scanning for open ice. Obstacles and coaches can be added to force players to keep their eyes up while handling.
coaching_points: Keep the head up as much as possible.
Shoulder-check before changing direction.
Find open ice before turning.
Reduce the space or shorten whistle intervals for advanced groups.

title: 2 vs. 2 2 Ways Game
description: One pair attacks 2-on-2 into one end while a second 2-on-2 begins toward the opposite end. On the whistle, the players from the first game sprint down to join the second game, creating a 4-on-4 finish.
coaching_points: Defense holds the blue line with active sticks.
Forwards enter with possession or controlled chips instead of blind dumps.
Transition quickly when the whistle changes the game.
Compete through the conditioning element.

title: Circle Warm Up Series
description: Players use the markings of a faceoff circle for a menu of skating and puckhandling movements, including stops, tight turns, escapes, pivots, backward work, one-touch passing and overspeed wheeling.
coaching_points: Underhandle the puck.
Keep the head up.
Communicate before passes.
Choose only the movements that fit the group and practice goal.
Use the circle lines to demand precise footwork.

title: Half Ice Slalom Races
description: Two players race through a slalom course, complete a full control turn around the last obstacle and compete for a coach-spotted 50/50 puck. The first player to win it attacks while the second immediately becomes the backchecking defender.
coaching_points: Stay low and fast through the slalom.
Execute the final control turn tightly.
Compete through the loose puck.
Winner transitions directly to offense.
Second player backchecks immediately.

title: Peanut Skating Drill with Pivots (Half Ice)
description: Players follow the classic peanut route around the two circles but add forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward pivots at designated points, forcing continuous edge control and directional changes.
coaching_points: Rotate the chest toward the inside dot on forward crossovers.
Always pivot toward the inside dot.
Use a strong backward cross-under.
Keep speed through every transition.

title: Max Skill Station Series #1 - #3
description: A compact skill station built around a tire, a short barrier and a net. The three progressions combine control turns, puck retrievals, single shifts, backward-to-forward transitions and quick shooting from tight space.
coaching_points: Keep control turns tight and balanced.
Pull retrieved pucks into the body so they are ready to shoot.
Protect the puck when shifting around the barrier.
Progress from forward retrievals to backward retrievals and transitions.

title: Wall Retrieval Station
description: A player times a wall retrieval on a rimmed puck, gathers it while moving up ice, passes to the next player in line, loops around an obstacle and receives the puck back for a shot.
coaching_points: Move the feet through the wall pickup.
Get to the wall before collecting the rim.
Scan the point before and during the retrieval.
After gaining possession, create space off the wall before making the next play.

title: Pad Skating with Pass and Shot
description: Players retrieve a puck from one net, perform a chosen skating or puckhandling skill around pads or cones, pass to a corner teammate, receive the return pass and finish with a shot.
coaching_points: Use the obstacle section to emphasize the day's skating skill.
Keep the head up while handling through the pads.
Pass and receive in stride.
Rotate the shooter into the passing role after the rep.

title: Full Ice Skating & Skills with 9 Variations
description: A full-ice cone setup for repeated edgework and puck-control patterns. The listed variations include stops and starts, tight turns, figure eights, forward-to-backward transitions and mohawks, with or without a puck.
coaching_points: Use the full ice to accelerate between skill zones.
Stay low and controlled at the cones.
Perform the same pattern both directions.
Add pucks only after the skating mechanics are clean.

title: Puck Stack Races
description: Teams race from the goal line to build a tower of pucks directly on the blue line. Each player carries one puck by hand, stacks it on the tower and races back to tag the next teammate.
coaching_points: Explode with full strides to and from the blue line.
Stay under control when placing the puck.
Keep the stack on the actual blue line.
Add backward skating or obstacles as a progression.

title: 2 on 1 to 3 on 2 High Man Backcheck
description: The sequence begins with a 2-on-1. A third forward then joins to create the next 3-on-2, and after that rush the high forward becomes the backchecker on the following 2-on-1.
coaching_points: Defense keeps sticks in passing lanes and forces play outside.
Forwards communicate and support the puck.
Backchecker uses long strides through middle ice.
Transition quickly between the 2-on-1 and 3-on-2 phases.

title: Box Tag
description: Players stay inside a small box or circle while one tagger tries to eliminate them. The confined space naturally forces tight turns, weight shifts and quick directional changes.
coaching_points: Use deception and weight shifts to escape the tagger.
Stay low through tight turns.
Keep scanning for open space.
Increase the space for more speed or add extra taggers for difficulty.

title: 2 V 0 to 2 v 2 Full Ice Backcheck
description: A pair attacks full ice 2-on-0. As soon as that rush ends, the next pair attacks the opposite direction while the first two players immediately transition into full-ice backcheckers.
coaching_points: Attackers use full strides and underhandle the puck.
Shoot in stride or use a quick pass-and-release.
Backcheckers recover through middle ice with sticks down.
Communicate assignments while closing the rush.

title: 1 v 1 Skating Race - Pick 3 Turns
description: Two players race into a four-cone area, choose any three cones for tight turns, then compete for a loose puck and finish with a shot on goal.
coaching_points: Get low and load the edges through each turn.
Look toward the exit of the turn.
Keep the feet moving immediately after every turn.
Compete through the puck after the third turn.

title: 3 Speed Warm-Up Drill
description: Every player has a puck and reacts to whistle changes: 50% speed with skates staying on the ice, 75% with creative turns and lateral movement, then 100% explosive skating into open space.
coaching_points: Keep the head up at every speed.
Use wide lateral puck movement at the slow speed.
Be creative at the middle speed.
At full speed, push outside the comfort zone while still scanning.

title: Chase The Rabbit
description: Players work in pairs inside a defined area. The Rabbit moves without a puck using pivots, tight turns and traffic, while the Chaser follows as closely as possible while handling a puck.
coaching_points: Both players keep their heads up in traffic.
Rabbit changes direction and skating posture frequently.
Chaser controls the puck without staring down.
For advanced groups, give both players pucks.

title: Billy Purcell Off the Wall
description: A pass-and-follow warm-up runs down the ice. Each receiver jumps off the wall toward the dots before making the next pass, and the sequence finishes with a shot at the far end.
coaching_points: Get off the wall to create usable space.
Catch and pass on both forehand and backhand.
Keep the head up before receiving.
Move into the space of the player you just passed to.

title: Triangle Tag
description: Every skater has a puck while designated taggers move without sticks. Tagged players freeze and form a triangle with their stick and skates; teammates can untag them by stickhandling through the triangle.
coaching_points: Keep the head up to identify taggers and open ice.
Use tight turns and changes of direction to escape.
Protect the puck while helping teammates.
Shrink the area or add taggers to increase difficulty.

title: Half Way Around The World - Head On
description: Both groups carry pucks around two offset nets and travel head-on through shared space. The goal is not to race but to force players to handle the puck while identifying moving traffic.
coaching_points: Head stays up throughout the drill.
Treat the oncoming group as moving obstacles.
Do not turn it into a speed race.
Add figure-eight crossings only after players can safely scan and handle.

title: Gretzky 2 V 2 Switch Game
description: Two active players per team play in the middle with a support player behind the offensive net. The behind-net support can switch with an active teammate at any time as long as one player remains below the goal line, creating exchanges and new attacking options.
coaching_points: Use give-and-go plays and switches to create space.
Behind-net support scans before receiving and uses the net as protection.
Defenders keep heads on a swivel and sticks in passing lanes.
Communicate every switch so spacing stays organized.

title: Race to 2 vs. 2 Game
description: Two players from each team race around separate cones after the coach chips a puck into the zone. The first team to the puck gains possession and the play immediately becomes a live 2-on-2.
coaching_points: Explode off the line and communicate which cone each player will take.
Winning team spreads into support positions immediately.
Defenders identify assignments quickly after losing the race.
Keep shifts short and competitive.

title: 7 Pass Transition Shooting Drill
description: One player works through a seven-pass sequence with players on both sides of the ice, transitions around two cones while facing the puck, receives the final pass and quickly shoots.
coaching_points: Pass flat with soft hands.
Face the puck through every transition.
Receive and release quickly after the final pass.
Follow the shot to the net for rebounds.

title: Tire Turns Progression Skating Station
description: Four stations progress from a basic control turn, to forward-to-backward transition, to a quick return to forward, and finally two tight control turns in opposite directions.
coaching_points: Master the basic control turn before progressing.
Stay low and balanced through transitions.
Keep turns tight around the tire.
Use the station that matches each player's current level.

title: Continuous Warm Up Skills Series #3
description: Players make one-touch passes down the ice, then carry the puck through an outside-turn sequence using three crossovers one way and three the other before continuing the warm-up flow.
coaching_points: Receive and pass quietly without slapping at the puck.
Keep the head up while carrying.
Drive the crossovers instead of coasting.
Maintain flow and spacing between groups.

title: Finnish Footwork Shooting Drill
description: Players work explosive backward starts, transitions to the wall for a coach-fed retrieval, controlled return passes, another backward transition around the dot and a final pass into shooting position.
coaching_points: Explode on backward starts.
Make the first-touch return pass under control.
Show the stick as a target after each transition.
Pull the final pass into shooting position in one motion.
Drive the net for a rebound.

title: Backwards Give and Go Station #1
description: A player starts backward with a puck, transitions forward around the first cone, passes to the next player and receives a quick return, then circles the second cone and finishes with a shot.
coaching_points: Control the puck while skating backward.
Transition forward without losing speed.
Make the give-and-go pass crisp and immediately get available again.
Finish with feet moving into the shot.

title: One Player Transition Drill
description: A player transitions backward to receive from the coach, controls the puck while skating up the wall, passes to the next player, moves outside the blue line, transitions backward again and receives the return before attacking the net.
coaching_points: Present a clear target and communicate.
Keep the feet moving throughout the rep.
Face the puck during transitions.
Control the return pass before attacking the net.

title: Half Ice Skating & Pucks
description: Two groups skate around four obstacles arranged near the faceoff circles, retrieve pucks at speed and attack their nets. The route can be changed to figure eights, transitions, stops and starts, or 360s.
coaching_points: Make tight turns and explode out of them.
Keep the head up during the puck pickup.
Maintain speed through the retrieval.
Use the competition to demand pace without sacrificing control.

title: NZ Pad Skating Race with Shot
description: Two players race around four pads in the neutral zone, then battle for a coach-spotted puck. The winner attacks the net while the second player applies back pressure.
coaching_points: Accelerate out of every tight turn.
Use body position to win the puck race.
Protect the puck on the way to the net.
Vary the skating route with forward/backward transitions or jumps.

title: Glide Turn and Shooting Drill
description: A player glides into the first cone, accelerates into a second glide turn, then receives a pass from the corner and shoots quickly while continuing toward the net.
coaching_points: Use a wide base with the inside foot leading around the turn.
Accelerate out of the glide.
Keep the stick ready as a passing target.
Release quickly after receiving the pass.

title: Angling Transition 1 v 1 to 2 v 1
description: A puck carrier crosses the neutral zone while a defender angles from the far side. Whichever player wins the objective activates a teammate, turning the play into a quick 2-on-1 while the losing player transitions to defense.
coaching_points: Angler matches speed and protects middle ice.
Keep the stick on the ice to take away lanes.
Puck carrier protects and cuts back if the middle opens.
Transition immediately once the 2-on-1 is activated.

title: Gate Game
description: Two teams play in a small area containing several cone gates. A point is earned by passing through a gate to a teammate, forcing constant movement, communication and support away from the puck.
coaching_points: Move to open space instead of standing beside a gate.
Find clean passing lanes before forcing the puck.
Communicate verbally and with stick position.
Defenders pursue with sticks in lanes and transition immediately after a takeaway.

title: 2 V 2 Any Net Game
description: A 2-on-2 is played with two scoring nets and three outside support players. A team must use an outside support option after gaining possession before it can attack either net.
coaching_points: Scan constantly because both nets are live.
Jump to open space after using a support player.
Communicate before and during each shift.
Defenders win possession, find support and transition immediately.

title: Offensive Zone 4 Shot
description: One player works through four scoring actions: an obstacle attack and shot, a second puck with a tight turn and shot, a corner retrieval around the net for a slot shot, and a final quick-release or one-timer from a coach's pass.
coaching_points: Keep the head up through the obstacles.
Feet stay active out of the corners and turns.
Use quick releases rather than overhandling.
Finish every puck and stay ready for the next one.

title: Tic Tac Toe Relay
description: Two teams skate through an obstacle course and place a team object on a large Tic Tac Toe grid before racing back to tag the next player. The relay continues until one team completes the game.
coaching_points: Use the obstacle course to emphasize the day's skating skill.
Race back through the line before tagging the next player.
Players must think about the Tic Tac Toe strategy while skating under pressure.
Keep the game competitive and fast.

title: Defensive Transition Passing
description: A three-part progression develops passing while skating backward, escape moves with the puck and transitions up ice while continuing to face the puck.
coaching_points: Keep the head up.
Present a clear target to the passer.
Face the puck through the transition.
Add moving passers or obstacles after the basic footwork is clean.

title: Golden Cross
description: A demanding half-ice sequence that begins with an Iron Cross, moves into backward passing across the top of the zone, then adds a puck pickup, power turn, give-and-go and quick shot.
coaching_points: Execute every stop and start with full effort.
Stay balanced while receiving passes backward.
Explode out of the power turn.
Make the give-and-go quickly and finish with a fast release.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #8
description: Two players skate around the net, work through a figure-eight pattern around two tires, use crossovers to build speed around the outside and then race through the middle for a loose puck.
coaching_points: Use tight turns around the tires.
Keep the feet moving through the figure eight.
Accelerate with crossovers before the final puck race.
Compete all the way through possession.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #7
description: Players race through a triangle of tires, repeatedly transitioning forward-to-backward and backward-to-forward before opening the hips and competing for a loose puck.
coaching_points: Make every transition efficient and balanced.
Stay low while skating backward.
Open the hips cleanly on the final transition.
Explode into the puck race after the final tire.

title: Quarter Ice Puck Race #6
description: Two players race forward around four tires arranged as a square, completing two laps before sprinting through the middle for a loose puck and scoring chance.
coaching_points: Use powerful crossovers to create speed.
Stay outside the tires and keep the route honest.
Keep the feet moving through both laps.
Explode through the middle when the puck race begins.

title: Merrimack Wall Drill
description: A coach rims the puck around the boards and the player meets it on the wall with the head up. The player reads a coach's pressure position, either protects up the wall or cuts to middle ice, then attacks around the line and shoots.
coaching_points: Time the rim so the puck is controlled cleanly off the wall.
Scan before and during the retrieval.
React to pressure instead of predetermining the escape.
Accelerate after the decision and release the shot quickly.

title: 1 v 1 Three Gates Game
description: One attacker and one defender compete inside a faceoff circle containing three gates. The puck carrier scores by carrying from inside the circle through a gate; a turnover immediately changes which player is on offense.
coaching_points: Offense uses skating and deception to win space.
Protect the puck with body position.
Defense keeps the stick on the puck and angles away from gates.
After a turnover, create space immediately.

title: Neutral Zone Game with Outlets
category: Neutral Zone / Small Area Game / Outlets
description: Play 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 in the neutral zone with one stationary outlet available to each team. Players may use the outlet when it helps, creating fast support decisions and quick-touch scoring opportunities.
coaching_points: Identify whether the outlet actually improves the play.
Move into open space after every pass.
Use quick touches and fast releases.
Keep scanning because the support option can change the pressure picture immediately.

title: Long Bomb
category: Neutral Zone / Small Area Game / Fast Break
description: Play 2-on-2 or 3-on-3 between two moved-up nets. A team can send the puck behind its own goal line to activate a fresh puck from the coach at center, creating instant long-pass and breakaway opportunities.
coaching_points: Players without the puck decide whether to support or stretch for the new puck.
Communicate before activating the long-bomb option.
Defenders scan away from the puck for breaking threats.
Use the reset option instead of forcing a bad play.

title: Battle Dome 1 on 1
description: A 1-on-1 begins with an offensive rim retrieval in a tight corner area with the net angled toward the battle. The offense works off the wall to create a scoring chance while the defender angles, uses an active stick and wins body position.
coaching_points: Offense gets off the wall and uses deception to create space.
Protect the puck before trying to make a play.
Defense maintains a useful angle and stick-on-puck pressure.
Use strong body position without chasing behind the play.

title: Fran Gow 3 on 2 or 3 on 3
category: Wall Play / Retrievals / Small Area Game
description: Three attackers work against two or three defenders on three consecutive rimmed pucks. Offense must control unpredictable wall retrievals and attack the net while defenders apply immediate pressure and box out.
coaching_points: Control rims cleanly and get off the wall.
Use cutbacks, jab steps and puck protection to create time.
Attack the net with purpose instead of staying on the perimeter.
Defenders maintain stick-on-puck pressure and win inside body position.

title: 3 vs 2 Three Pucks Game
description: Three attackers play against two defenders and a goalie inside a confined area. The coach feeds three separate pucks in rapid succession, giving the offense three scoring chances while the defenders must repeatedly reset and protect the middle.
coaching_points: Offense attacks quick 2-on-1 opportunities inside the 3-on-2.
Create traffic and rebound chances at the net.
Defenders communicate and identify the most dangerous attacker.
Protect middle ice and remove backdoor passing lanes.

title: 2 on 2 Angle Game
description: Two players retrieve below the goal line while two opponents establish forechecking angles. If the forecheck creates a turnover, a third attacking player joins, producing a quick 3-on-2 before the rep ends.
coaching_points: F1 pressures immediately with speed and a useful angle.
F2 supports the forecheck instead of chasing the same lane.
Use stick-on-puck pressure to create the turnover.
After possession changes, transition quickly into the 3-on-2.

title: 1 v 1 Through Gates
description: A live 1-on-1 where each player attacks the opponent's gate. Players score by carrying the puck through the gate, so possession changes instantly flip offense and defense.
coaching_points: Defender keeps a tight gap, watches the player and forces outside.
Keep the stick on the ice to close lanes.
Offense uses body position, deception and dekes to create space.
Make gates smaller or the area tighter to increase difficulty.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: Defend The Gate
description: The attacker starts ahead with the puck and tries to reach a gate while the trailing defender works to angle the puck carrier outside and prevent the middle attack.
coaching_points: Defender wins with body angle and stick position rather than chasing the puck.
Match the attacker's speed before closing.
Offense protects the puck and uses deception to gain middle ice.
Change gate size to adjust difficulty.
source_license_note: Content licensed from the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF).

title: Corner Houda
description: A rim starts a live corner battle. The offensive group retrieves and attacks while the defenders protect structure, then the defensive group must skate or pass the puck out to transition. The format can scale from 3-on-3 into 5-on-3 or 5-on-4 special-teams work.
coaching_points: Win the wall retrieval with body position and communication.
Defenders maintain layers, net-front coverage and sticks in lanes.
Offense creates quickly after gaining the rim.
Use different manpower situations to teach d-zone, PP and PK habits.

title: 2 on 2 Net to Corner
description: A 2-on-2 battle is played in a tight corner with the net angled toward the middle. After each possession change, the new attacking team must tag the puck back behind the goal-line boundary before attacking again.
coaching_points: Use body position to shield the puck along the wall.
Shoulder-check before receiving or escaping pressure.
Make quick give-and-go plays instead of holding the puck.
Defenders pressure the puck and anticipate the next play.

title: 2 v 0 High Roll
description: One player rims the puck down the wall. The low player picks it cleanly off the boards, gets off the wall, meets the original passer for a switch, then rolls high into space for a return pass and in-stride shot.
coaching_points: Absorb the rim and move off the wall immediately.
Time the switch so both players keep speed.
High roll creates separation and a clear passing lane.
Catch and release the final pass without breaking stride.

title: Pearl 4 v 2 Game
description: A cross-ice 4-on-2 special-teams game uses a scoring system that rewards power-play goals, one-timers and shorthanded goals. Teams alternate which group receives the power play.
coaching_points: Power play supports the puck with multiple outlets and moves it faster than the PK can recover.
Penalty killers keep sticks in lanes and angle play outside.
Swarm loose pucks after turnovers.
Change the scoring system to reward the skill or behavior you want.

title: The Backcheck Game
description: A high-tempo cross-ice game begins 2-on-0 with two opponents backchecking. When the backcheckers win the puck, they break out fresh teammates waiting in the neutral-zone lane to attack the other way.
coaching_points: Offense attacks quickly and looks for shots off the pass.
Backcheckers keep sticks in lanes and angle attackers.
After a takeaway, lift the head and find the breakout option.
The shift naturally flows offense to backcheck to defense to breakout.

title: 1 v 1 to 2 v 2 (Stick vs No Stick)
description: The progression starts with a corner 1-on-1 and then adds the opposite pair to create 2-on-2. Defenders can begin without a usable stick to force proper footwork, angle and body position before progressing to normal stick use.
coaching_points: Defender wins with feet, angle and body position before relying on the stick.
Offense retrieves the loose puck and attacks under pressure.
Progress from no stick, to an inverted stick, to normal stick use.
When the drill becomes 2-on-2, communicate and sort coverage quickly.

title: Breakaway Backcheck With 1 on 1 Variation
description: The offensive player starts with a step while the defender has the better angle to the net. They race through a live backcheck battle, and the progression can add a defenseman so the same rep becomes a 1-on-1 with a backchecker.
coaching_points: Backchecker takes the direct angle and works through the hands, not only the puck.
Offensive player cuts off the defender and protects inside ice.
Win body position before trying to win possession.
Use the second progression to combine rush defense with back pressure.

title: Bourque 3 on 3 Game
category: 3 on 3 / Breakout Support / Small Area Game
description: Three-on-three is played cross-ice with a designated support player behind each team's own goal line. After every possession change, the team must use its 'Bourque' to initiate the breakout before it can attack.
coaching_points: Support player behind the net makes a clean first pass.
Use deception to move forecheckers before the breakout.
Players return underneath the puck to support the Bourque.
Fill three lanes and attack open ice after the breakout.

title: 1 v 1 Angle Around The Net Drill
description: A defenseman retrieves a chipped puck and must escape through a gate while a forechecker starts on the coach's signal and tries to angle, strip the puck and score.
coaching_points: Forechecker keeps the stick down, matches speed and takes the correct route.
Retriever shoulder-checks before arriving at the puck.
Retrieve at an angle to preserve speed.
Use deception with skates, hips, shoulders and stick to shake pressure.

title: Back to Back 1 vs 1 with Mini Nets
category: 1 on 1 / Puck Protection / Small Area Game
description: Two mini nets sit back-to-back inside a small playing area. A coach dumps in a puck and two players battle for possession, with either net available as a scoring target.
coaching_points: Protect the puck before attacking a net.
Use tight turns and changes of direction to escape pressure.
Scan because either net can be attacked.
Keep shifts short and continuously reload pucks after goals or exits.

title: 2 vs 2 Rebound Battle Drill
description: The goalie plays an initial puck to a corner and two players race to win it. The winner must find a point player, which turns the play into a live 2-on-1; a progression can activate the second point player to make it 2-on-2.
coaching_points: First player to the puck uses deception and body position to escape the corner.
Get the head up and find the point quickly.
Defender protects middle ice and keeps a stable stick position.
Point player stays active as a passing target.

title: King or Queen of the Hill Puck Control Drill
description: Every player starts with a puck inside a defined area and tries to keep possession while knocking opponents' pucks away. Eliminated players leave until one player remains.
coaching_points: Protect your own puck before attacking someone else's.
Keep the head up to scan for pressure.
Use body position and controlled stick checks.
Shrink the area as players are eliminated to raise difficulty.

title: 5 v 5 Neutral Zone Face-Off Possession Game
description: Teams begin with a neutral-zone faceoff and compete to carry the puck through scoring gates on the red line. Different gates can be worth different points, so players must support possession and recognize the best attacking lane.
coaching_points: Support the puck carrier with clear outlets.
Defend middle ice first and keep sticks in lanes.
Communicate through the faceoff and possession change.
Use the scoring gates to reward controlled entries rather than hopeful passes.

title: Wing Quadrant Play
description: A 3-on-3 is played on one side of the zone with a defined winger quadrant. The winger's job is to prevent the puck carrier from skating through that area while still reacting quickly to point passes.
coaching_points: Winger protects the quadrant first and angles play outside.
Keep the stick down to block lanes.
Close quickly when the puck reaches the point.
Communicate with the defenseman and opposite winger when coverage changes.

title: Go Go
description: A corner battle begins 1-on-1. Each time the coach calls 'Go,' the next player from alternating teams enters, creating changing situations such as 2-on-1, 2-on-2, 3-on-2 and 3-on-3.
coaching_points: First attacker protects the puck and gets off the wall.
New players jump in immediately as support.
Defense communicates as the numbers change.
Keep the pace high so players must recognize new situations quickly.

title: 2 on 2 Angling with Defensive Reward
description: Two attackers rush two defenders in half ice. If the defenders create a quick turnover, a third teammate is activated to reward the defensive play and create a 3-on-2 transition the other way.
coaching_points: Defenders steer attackers into low-risk ice.
Match speed before closing the gap.
Keep sticks on the ice to remove passing lanes.
Activated third player jumps into the play immediately and communicates.

title: Owls 2 v 2
description: A three-part battle progression starts with net-front box-outs on a point shot, moves into an in-zone 2-on-2, then finishes with a full-ice 2-on-2 or 3-on-2 rush.
coaching_points: Forwards battle for inside net-front position.
Defenders eliminate sticks and clear the goalie's sightline.
Transition quickly when the second and third pucks are introduced.
If using the 3-on-2 variation, the third forward joins at full speed.

title: Purple Eagle Angle Drill
description: Players pass across the neutral-zone dots, then the passer immediately becomes the angler while the receiver attacks up ice. The puck carrier works to protect the puck and gain inside ice before shooting.
coaching_points: Defender keeps the stick down and steers the rush outside.
Puck carrier keeps the head up and protects through the defender's hands.
Attack middle ice after entering the zone.
Shoot in stride or change the shooting angle.

title: Cutting Hands Warm-Up
description: A puck carrier moves up the wall while a backchecker angles in, lifts the stick and takes possession. The new puck carrier then uses deception, escapes back up ice and practices protecting the puck through the defender's hands.
coaching_points: Backchecker approaches on a useful angle rather than directly from behind.
Separate the player from the puck before taking possession.
Use a deceptive escape immediately after the takeaway.
Puck carrier gets off the wall and protects with body position.

title: Beaver Track
description: One forward carries at controlled speed while a second player tracks, angles and steals the puck. The tracking player then moves the puck to a defenseman as a regroup outlet and joins the original forward for a 2-on-0 attack.
coaching_points: Tracker takes a hard inside-out route and attacks the hands.
Communicate through the turnover and regroup.
Keep sticks available as passing targets.
Transition from takeaway to offense immediately.

title: The Breakout Game
description: A five-player breakout unit retrieves a coach dump while a smaller forechecking group pressures. The breakout team tries to exit cleanly and score on the far net; the forecheckers are rewarded more heavily for creating a turnover and scoring.
coaching_points: Defense supports its partner on retrievals.
Center comes low as a clear outlet and wingers recover into breakout spots.
Forecheckers angle to the wall with sticks in lanes.
Scale the number of forecheckers to match the group's breakout ability.

title: Cloverleaf Drill
description: A puck carrier skates a cloverleaf route around a center marker and four outside markers while a defender follows with passive stick pressure. The route creates repeated chances to use body position and tight turns.
coaching_points: Stay low through every turn.
Use body position to create separation from the defender.
Protect through the defender's hands instead of only moving the puck.
Run reps without pressure first when players are learning the route.

title: Renegade Line Rush
description: The first whistle starts a tight 3-on-2 around a turned net. The second whistle sends the puck to a forward outside the battle, and the same players expand into a full 5-on-5 rush up ice.
coaching_points: Defense communicates and sorts coverage quickly in tight space.
Offense attacks immediately on the first puck.
On the second whistle, move the puck forward through the blue line and enter inside the dots.
Net drive and tracking continue into the 5-on-5 rush.
